In #40033, I replaced two uses of simp; infer_instance with explicit proofs to remove flexible linter suppressions. Should the linter accept simp; infer_instance, or should I keep the explicit proofs?

@Michael Rothgang , do you know which behavior was intended?

https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/40033
infer_instance was intentionally considered flexible, as discussed here: #mathlib4 > flexible vs rigid tactics

There was not much discussion, but the fact that some simp lemmas transform something that is a typeclass to a goal that is not one (i.e., simp can potentially break infer_instance proofs) encourages to not mark infer_instance as flexible.
Personally, I think that simp; infer_instance is rare enough that we can manually disable the linter in the few cases where it occurs.

In general, removing the suppression should be balanced with not making the proofs worse. (This is why the suppressions were added in the first place: if we found a nice proof back then, we could commit that instead.) In this case, I'm somewhat on the fence. The second file's changes look like improvements to me, the first... oh well.
